why: Each item's discount is the first item to its right with price <= its own: that is the classic 'next smaller-or-equal element' query, answered for all items in one pass with a monotonic stack.
hints: For each item you need the nearest later item that is not more expensive. Brute force is O(n^2) with n = 10^5.
Keep a stack of indices still waiting for their discount. When a new price p arrives, every waiting item with price >= p has just found its discount p; pop them.
One left-to-right pass with an index stack: pop while prices[top] >= p, set discount[top] = p, push i. Whatever stays on the stack is sold at full price. O(n) time.
pitfalls: The condition is equal OR lower, so pop on >=, not >.
The full-price list must be indices in ascending order, not the order they are left on the stack (that happens to be ascending, but do not reverse it).
The total can reach 10^5 * 10^9 = 10^14; use 64-bit integers outside Python.
Return strings: the total as a string and the indices joined by single spaces (empty string if none).
